    Biserial canonical projectives of a finite category algebra #

    The canonical projector attached to an object of a finite linear category is primitive when that object's endomorphism ring is local. The direct coordinate-thin biserial induction therefore applies to its principal right ideal.

    If all indecomposable modules over a finite category algebra are thin in the canonical coordinates, then every canonical principal right projective is biserial.

    Under the finite-category projective-generator equivalence, every covariant representable is biserial when all indecomposable algebra modules are thin in the canonical coordinates.
